options: Upper border of the spine of the scapula
Anterior (costal) surface of the medial border of the scapula
Posterior surface of the medial border of the scapula
mu-0c9254f5.explanation: Serratus anterior arises by digitations from the upper 8–9 ribs and inserts into the anterior surface of the medial border of the scapula, its thickest fibres to the inferior angle. It holds the scapula against the chest wall and protracts it; its lower fibres rotate the scapula upwards, helping the arm rise above 90°.

mu-4e87fa71.stem: Where does pectoralis minor arise and insert?
options: Arises from the clavicle and sternum, inserts into the crest of the greater tubercle
Arises from the 1st rib and its cartilage, inserts into the underside of the clavicle
Arises from ribs 2–5, inserts into the acromion
Arises from ribs 1–8, inserts into the medial border of the scapula
Arises from ribs 3–5, inserts into the coracoid process
mu-4e87fa71.explanation: Pectoralis minor is the landmark dividing the axillary artery into three parts. The other options describe pectoralis major, subclavius and serratus anterior; no chest muscle attaches to the acromion.
notes: This describes pectoralis major.
This describes subclavius.
No chest muscle attaches to the acromion.
This describes serratus anterior.

mu-b1ae9f59.stem: Which of the following does NOT act as an accessory muscle of respiration in forced inspiration?
mu-b1ae9f59.explanation: In forced inspiration muscles that raise the rib cage assist: SCM, the scalenes, pectoralis minor (with the arm fixed) and serratus posterior superior. The anterior abdominal wall muscles raise intra-abdominal pressure and act in forced expiration and coughing.

mu-006eef76.stem: What are the vertebral levels of the caval, oesophageal and aortic openings of the diaphragm, respectively?
mu-006eef76.explanation: The inferior vena cava passes through the central tendon at T8, the oesophagus and vagal trunks through the muscle fibres of the right crus at T10, and the aorta behind the diaphragm (under the median arcuate ligament) at T12. Memory aid: 'I ate ten eggs at twelve' (IVC 8, oesophagus 10, aorta 12).

mu-e1e57606.stem: Which structures pass through the oesophageal hiatus?
options: Oesophagus, vagal trunks and oesophageal branches of the left gastric artery and vein
Inferior vena cava and branches of the right phrenic nerve
Aorta, thoracic duct and azygos vein
mu-e1e57606.explanation: The oesophageal opening lies at T10 between the muscle fibres of the right crus; with the oesophagus pass the anterior and posterior vagal trunks and the oesophageal branches of the left gastric vessels. The ring formed by the muscle fibres acts like a physiological sphincter, and hiatus hernia develops here.
notes: It passes through the caval opening.
They pass behind or through the crura.
They pass through the aortic hiatus.
It passes through the sternocostal triangle (Larrey).

mu-61d192f5.stem: Which statement about the external intercostals is true?
options: Their fibres run vertically; they act only in coughing
Their fibres run downwards and forwards; they raise the ribs in inspiration
They extend as muscle in front as far as the sternum
Their fibres run downwards and backwards; they lower the ribs in expiration
The intercostal neurovascular bundle runs just deep to this muscle
mu-61d192f5.explanation: The external intercostals run downwards and forwards in the 'hands in pockets' direction and raise the ribs in inspiration; in front, between the cartilages, they become the external intercostal membrane. The internal intercostals run downwards and backwards. The neurovascular bundle lies between the internal and innermost intercostals.
notes: There is no such muscle.
In front they become the external intercostal membrane.
This describes the internal intercostals.
The bundle lies between the internal and innermost intercostals.

options: It runs from the transverse processes of the vertebrae to the ribs below
It forms the deepest muscle layer of the anterior abdominal wall
It runs near the angles of the ribs, skipping one or two intercostal spaces
It lies at the root of the neck above the 1st rib
It runs from the back of the sternum to the inner surfaces of costal cartilages 2–6
mu-720029f9.explanation: Transversus thoracis is a thin muscle on the inner surface of the anterior chest wall, behind the internal thoracic artery and vein; it is regarded as the thoracic continuation of transversus abdominis. Two of the other descriptions fit the subcostal muscles and the levatores costarum.

mu-1742f5c6.stem: What does the linea semilunaris indicate?
options: The lateral border of the rectus sheath
The medial end of the inguinal ligament
The midline separating the two recti
The lower limit of the posterior layer of the rectus sheath
mu-1742f5c6.explanation: The linea semilunaris is the curved line along the lateral border of the rectus sheath where the aponeuroses of the flat muscles meet; the gallbladder projects onto it at the tip of the ninth costal cartilage. The lower limit of the posterior layer is the arcuate line, and the midline is the linea alba.

mu-9d61e293.stem: Where is a Spigelian hernia most often found?
options: Along the linea semilunaris, at the level of the arcuate line
In the linea alba above the umbilicus
mu-9d61e293.explanation: A Spigelian hernia develops through the weak point of the transversus abdominis aponeurosis at the edge of rectus (Spigelian fascia), mostly at the level of the arcuate line where the posterior rectus sheath ends. Because it lies beneath the external oblique aponeurosis, it can be hard to feel.
notes: This is the site of umbilical hernia.
This is the site of direct inguinal hernia.
This is the site of epigastric hernia.
This is the site of lumbar hernia.

mu-8303ae76.stem: Which is the deepest of the three flat muscles of the anterolateral abdominal wall?
mu-8303ae76.explanation: From superficial to deep: external oblique (downwards and forwards), internal oblique (upwards and forwards) and transversus abdominis (horizontal). Beneath transversus lie the transversalis fascia and peritoneum; its deep fibres act as a 'corset' raising intra-abdominal pressure.

mu-e07158a3.stem: Above the arcuate line, which structures form the posterior layer of the rectus sheath?
options: All the aponeuroses of the three flat muscles
The posterior lamina of the internal oblique aponeurosis and the transversus abdominis aponeurosis
The external and internal oblique aponeuroses
mu-e07158a3.explanation: Above the arcuate line the internal oblique aponeurosis splits: its anterior lamina joins the external oblique in the anterior sheath, its posterior lamina joins transversus in the posterior sheath. Below the arcuate line all three aponeuroses pass in front; only the transversalis fascia remains behind rectus.

mu-9b9c017a.stem: What is the function of pyramidalis?
options: It is the main flexor of the trunk
mu-9b9c017a.explanation: Pyramidalis is a small triangular muscle arising from the pubis and attaching to the linea alba; it lies within the rectus sheath, in front of rectus abdominis, and is absent in some people. It is supplied by the subcostal nerve (T12).

options: Posterior part of the iliac crest
Lower border of the 12th rib and transverse processes of L1–L4
Transverse process of L5 and iliolumbar ligament
mu-db78fc48.explanation: Quadratus lumborum arises from the posterior iliac crest and iliolumbar ligament and inserts into the 12th rib and upper lumbar transverse processes. It fixes the 12th rib in inspiration and, acting on one side, bends the trunk sideways. Psoas major arises from the vertebral bodies and inserts into the lesser trochanter.
notes: This is the muscle's origin.
This is the insertion of iliopsoas.
This is part of the muscle's origin.
This is the origin of psoas major.

mu-d71ee117.stem: Which muscles form the pelvic diaphragm?
options: External anal sphincter and deep transverse perineal muscle
mu-d71ee117.explanation: The pelvic floor (pelvic diaphragm) consists of the funnel-shaped levator ani (puborectalis, pubococcygeus, iliococcygeus) and coccygeus behind. Obturator internus and piriformis are in the lateral and posterior walls of the pelvis; bulbospongiosus and ischiocavernosus are superficial perineal muscles.

mu-8605eb53.stem: The tendinous arch from which levator ani arises is a thickening of the fascia of which muscle?
mu-8605eb53.explanation: Levator ani arises in front from the back of the pubis, behind from the ischial spine, and in between from the tendinous arch of levator ani formed by a thickening of the obturator internus fascia. So the upper part of obturator internus lies within the pelvis and its lower part in the perineum (lateral wall of the ischio-anal fossa).
